item.description: The Pro Padel League (PPL) and the hometown Las Vegas Smash partnered with P1 Padel to host a children’s clinic Tuesday, Nov. 17. item.title: Mets met with Tarik Skubal. These 5 teams will sit down with him next
item.description: Meetings with Tarik Skubal in free agency are underway and the Mets were first in line this week. A Mets contingent had an opportunity to sit down with Skubal’s camp and deliver an initial in-person pitch in California on Monday, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post. Chelsea Janes of SNY added that owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns were among those involved from New York, which doesn’t come as a surprise. So long as the Mets are in on Skubal, they will be considered a favorite. New York has a glaring need at the top of their rotation, so Skubal fits what they’re looking for this winter. He’d be an immediate upgrade, giving the Mets the ace that they’ve been looking for. The Mets are sitting at +108 to be Tarik Skubal’s next team on Kalshi . For a closer look, visit our guide to the best sportsbook promos to shop for odds. The Mets can also afford to sign a player of his caliber to a record-setting deal, which is what it’s going to take to snag him on the open market. While Stearns isn’t known for handing out long-term deals to pitchers because of the inherent injury risk, Cohen’s track record suggests that the Mets will be comfortable spending big to acquire the best player available. Mix in the urgency to bolster this roster after the way these last few disappointing seasons have unfolded and it makes even more sense for the Mets to go all out for Skubal. According to Heyman, the incumbent Dodgers, the Padres, Blue Jays and a pair of mystery teams were also granted meetings with the ace. Time will tell when those meetings occur, but they’re scheduled for this week, per Heyman. These meetings are just the first step in what’s poised to be a fast-paced process. Since only two weeks remain until the lockout is expected to begin (on December 1 at 11:59 p.m.), time is of the essence for teams to convince Skubal to pick them. Offers are pivotal, especially with a Scott Boras client, but as was the case with the Juan Soto sweepstakes, the Mets will need to recruit Skubal with information about their long-term outlook. item.title: Why Colts are still not giving Anthony Richardson Sr. a chance to start
item.description: Why Colts are still not giving Anthony Richardson Sr. a chance to start originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The 2026 NFL season for the Indianapolis Colts has been a complete disaster. They're headed for one of the top picks in the NFL draft, except the issue is that they already sent their 2027 first-rounder to the New York Jets for Sauce Gardner. With the Colts struggling to secure wins, even against the lowly Miami Dolphins , it wouldn't be a surprise if the Colts made some changes to the team this season. Benching Daniel Jones would seem to be a good option for the Colts. However, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler revealed why the Colts are not going to turn to Anthony Richardson Sr. this season, and it's quite a disappointing update for Colts fans. Why Anthony Richardson Sr. isn't going to be starting for the Colts anytime soon "As it was told to me, Steichen simply is not motivated to play Anthony Richardson Sr., the 2023 fourth overall pick who fell out of favor after a strong start to his rookie year," Fowler reports. The Colts have plenty of reason to bench Jones this season. He's been one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL, has led the team to a 3-7 record, and isn't giving the Colts much of a chance to win. But even with the clear offensive issues, the Colts are not going to make a QB change this season. And if they do, it might not even be a pivot to Richardson. Riley Leonard might be the QB1 in Indianapolis if the Colts end up benching Jones at some point this season. Shane Steichen seemingly has no plans to turn to Richardson this season. MORE : Grading NFL trade deadline debuts, from Kirk Cousins' Vikings return to Josh Downs' impressive day Will Jones ever be benched this season? As Fowler put it, "I just don't see Steichen benching Jones right now unless absolutely necessary." This Colts team isn't going to contend for a playoff spot, not after selling at the trade deadline. But without their own first-round pick, Steichen and the Colts will still be trying to win every week. That means the best QB for the job will get the starts, and as of now, that's Jones in the eyes of Steichen. While Richardson might be a higher-upside option and a much more exciting starter than Jones, Colts fans aren't likely to see the former No. 3 overall pick this season, despite now being the time to get a look at the quarterback. item.title: Stephen A. Smith issues warning to rest of NBA about Lakers: ‘These white brothers can play’
item.description: Stephen A. Smith issues warning to rest of NBA about Lakers: ‘These white brothers can play’ originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The early returns on LeBron James' decision to leave the Lakers for the 76ers are positive for all sides. While Philadelphia is off to a terrific start in the East, the Lakers don't look like they miss James at all. L.A. is off to a 13-2 start and still hasn't lost in November, with Luka Doncic playing at an MVP level. Count Stephen A. Smith among those who are starting to believe in the Lakers, though the nature of his comments Wednesday raised a few eyebrows among fans. Here's a look at what Smith had to say. MORE: Quentin Grimes steals the spotlight with 47-point performance Stephen A. Smith sends warning to rest of NBA about Lakers Smith heaped praise on the Lakers during "First Take" on Wednesday, calling Doncic "all-world" and giving credit to the jobs done by Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and coach JJ Redick. After previously criticizing the Lakers for building their roster around "three white dudes" during the summer, Smith then brought up the subject again. "I ain't never seen what they assembled, what they're being led by, deliver an NBA championship in my lifetime," Smith said. In case it wasn't clear what he was referring to, Smith laid it out. "These white brothers can play. They can play," Smith said. "They gonna win a championship? This is the NBA. Y'all gonna let them win a championship? Let's see. I'm not rooting against nobody." "I'm looking at the brothers, and I'm saying, LA doing special things…these white brothers can play, y'all gonna let them win a championship?" – Stephen A. Smith https://t.co/a18LzidzhR — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 18, 2026 After co-host Shae Cornette tried to move onto another topic, Smith insisted he was just curious about how the rest of the NBA will respond. "All I'm saying is, throughout NBA history it hasn't happened," Smith said. "What you gonna do about it?" MORE: 11 NBA midseason trade candidates After the Lakers acquired Walker Kessler in a sign-and-trade in July, Smith claimed the Lakers weren't "going anywhere" with "a bunch of white dudes" leading the way. "Where the hell do the Los Angeles Lakers thing they're going with a bunch of white dudes?" Smith asked. "Your three top players are white dudes? Really. This ain't golf. This ain't baseball." More than four months later, Smith might not be fully bought into the idea the Lakers can pull it off, but he seems to be coming around to the reality that L.A. has a roster that can compete for a championship. "It's a terrible feeling," Wembanyama said. "A terrible sight." The 20-year-old Harper was scheduled to undergo further testing Wednesday, leaving the Spurs to contemplate life without their second-leading scorer as they try to get another winning streak started. That effort begins Thursday, when the Los Angeles Clippers visit the Frost Bank Center. But because the recording on YouTube had to be broken up into multiple parts due to length, producing the correct tally proved challenging. With the previous record of 20.16 Murphs well within reach, Godbout was surprised that the counter on the video read “16” at 2 a.m. for the attempt that began at 9 a.m. the previous day, Nov. 13. His crew, consisting of girlfriend Abby Saner and workout buddy Paul Woods, needed to be sure. Murphy was killed in action in Afghanistan 21 years ago. He was posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor. The Murph Challenge fundraiser is held annually on Memorial Day. Godbout dedicated his effort to his grandfather, Tom McCarthy of Middleborough. item.title: NASCAR’s 200-Mph Clash Twist Adds Pit Stop Chaos
item.description: Scott Sewell-Imagn Images NASCAR is changing the game for the 2027 Clash at Daytona International Speedway. The sport is adding a qualifying twist that forces teams to pit during their fastest lap. Simulation models suggest speeds could hit 200 mph while crews swap four tires. This new format borrows from the All-Star Race rules but adds a Daytona-sized stress test. Under official supervision, a particular car configuration is required as teams traverse pit road. item.title: Sonny Gray Leaving Red Sox To Return To Twins
item.description: Minnesota Twins Pitcher Sonny Gray The Boston Red Sox are losing Sonny Gray to the Minnesota Twins. Skies are Gray but things are looking Sonny! Welcome back, Sonny Gray! pic.twitter.com/Ky2sBhVi57 — Minnesota Twins (@Twins) November 18, 2026 Gray's deal with the Twins is a two-year, $55 million pact that includes an opt-out after the first year, according to ESPN's Jeff Passan. He spent two seasons with the Twins before joining the St. Louis Cardinals in 2024. Gray has pitched 14 seasons in the big leagues and had one of his best seasons last season. He posted a 2.72 ERA in 169 innings of work with the Red Sox. It was the lowest ERA he has posted in a full season in his entire career. Gray's last All-Star appearance came with the Twins in 2023. He is 37 years old, and retirement was on the table for him this offseason. It makes sense that his deal includes an opt-out after the first year. As for the Red Sox, Craig Breslow has already noted that he likes the pitching depth the team has behind Garrett Crochet, Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle and Jake Bennett. “I think the rotation is in a really good place,” Breslow told MassLive's Chris Cotillo on Nov. 9. “I think it should be a strength of our 2027 team. Whether that’s through Garrett (Crochet) being healthy, the continued development of Payton (Tolle), Ranger (Suarez) being a steady, stalwart presence for us, Jake Bennett who emerged and Brayan Bello, who when he came back from being out on option, he looked reinvigorated and was effective in multiple different roles. And getting (Johan Oviedo), Kutter (Crawford) and Tanner (Houck) healthy, I think we should have options and we’ll have some competition.” More MLB: Brewers' Jackson Chourio Makes MLB History With Silver Slugger Award

item.title: What Are Braves Options To Improve Rotation After Sonny Gray Signs With Twins?
item.description: Atlanta Braves general manager and president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos The Atlanta Braves need starting pitching and Sonny Gray seemed like a perfect fit, but he is signing with the Minnesota Twins. Gray is a veteran pitcher who has maintained durability and has made fewer than 25 starts just four times in 14 years, and two of those seasons were the pandemic-shortened season and his rookie season. Atlanta is the closest city with a big league team to his home in Nashville, so it made sense geographically as well. Not to mention, he was great last season. With Gray off the board, the Braves need to ensure they land one or both of Freddy Peralta and Michael King. Right now, the Braves' only real trustworthy option in the rotation is Chris Sale. Grant Holmes, Spencer Schwellenbach, A.J. Smith-Schawver, Spencer Strider and Didier Fuentes are all options in the rotation, but have flaws. It's unclear if Strider can ever be the pitcher he was before injuries and Fuentes has not had success as a starter yet. All of the other options the Braves have are not really stars, and may not be guys a team wants to trot out to start games in October. Adding King or Peralta would be great, but if the Braves miss on them, they will have to pivot to guys like Clay Holmes, Casey Mize, Jack Flaherty or Tyler Mahle. Mahle was great for the Braves last season after they acquired him, and re-signing him would be a great move. Another option from last season that it would make sense to re-sign is Martín Pérez. The Braves have not really been linked to Tarik Skubal, but that's certainly a name that any team would love to add. It's going to take more than one move to create a World Series-worthy rotation in Atlanta, and with Gray no longer an option, there is more pressure on the front office to make a move. item.title: Saints Offensive Line Crumbles As Rookie Mason Murphy Steps In
item.description: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images The New Orleans Saints will likely start undrafted rookie Mason Murphy at right tackle against the Chicago Bears this Sunday. Two veteran linemen suffered knee injuries in the last week, leaving the team with no other option. Head coach Kellen Moore confirmed on Monday that Asim Richards is out for multiple games. Taliese Fuaga, the original starter, also missed time after hurting his knee in practice last Thursday. Richards was already struggling in pass protection before his injury. He had replaced Kelvin Banks Jr. at left tackle for the last two months. Now Murphy must fill the gap on the right side. The Bears know Murphy better than most teams because he spent his summer with Chicago. He played 88 snaps in three preseason games for the Bears before being released. That history gives Chicago a clear map of his strengths and flaws. Chicago Holds the Edge Montez Sweat and the Bears defense will target Murphy immediately. The rookie moves well for his 6-foot-5, 315-pound frame but lacks power. He also shows below-average technique when blocking. These are the exact weaknesses Chicago scouts studied all summer. Sports Mockery reported that the Bears signed Murphy as an undrafted rookie several months ago. They have the inside track on how to beat him. New Orleans ranks 27th in the league against the run this year. If the Bears force the Saints to pass more often, Murphy will have to hold up against a blitz-heavy defense. The Saints have lost five of their last seven games. Their offense has been inconsistent all season. Rookie quarterback Tyler Shough is still learning the speed of the NFL. A Critical Test for Both Sides The Bears enter this game with a 7-2 record and a bye week behind them. They beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 27-24 on Sunday, Nov. 8. Now they face a Saints team that sits at 3-6. The game takes place on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET at Soldier Field. A win here sets up a tough divisional matchup against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving. Chicago cannot afford to overlook the Saints just because of the records. An early turnover or a stalled drive could turn a comfortable game into a fourth-quarter headache. Ben Johnson has changed the expectations for this roster. The team is no longer just hoping to hang around. They are expected to beat teams like New Orleans and move forward. The Saints need to protect the football and sustain their drives to win. Defensively, they must limit explosive plays and pressure Caleb Williams. Yahoo Sports noted that Sunday’s matchup offers another chance for New Orleans to show improvement. The Bears will try to exploit the weak link in the Saints line while managing their own rotation.

item.title: UNF senior Kaili Doctor earns school's first volleyball Player of Year
item.description: University of North Florida senior outside hitter Kaili Doctor was named the ASUN Player of the Year on Nov. 18 in a vote of the league's coaches, the first such honor for Ospreys in the NCAA Division I Era that began in 2005. Doctor, a native of Pittsburgh, posted 511.5 points, 443 kills, 149 digs, 47 total blocks, 17 aces and a .297 hitting percentage. She led the Ospreys (16-10 and seeded third in the ASUN Tournament Nov. 19-22) to their best season since 2021. Other major ASUN awards were Grace Jones of Lipscomb (Defensive Player of the Year), Kelsey Schenck of Lipscomb (Setter of the Year), Maju Hildebrand of Florida Gulf Coast (Freshman of the Year) and Sarah Baldwin of Lipscomb (Coach of the Year). Doctor was joined on the first team by teammate Dakota Spurrier, a junior outside hitter from Cincinnati. Also on the first team was Jaley Young of Jacksonville University, a junior middle blocker from St. Louis. UNF players Yarmimar Francis Garay, Sofia Dawson and Emma Pohlmann made the second team, along with Abby Tuyo of Jacksonville. The Dolphins Jaylyn Tuiasosopo made the All-Freshman team. UNF will play No. 6 seed Queens (9-18) in the first round of the ASUN Tournament at the Alico Arena in Fort Myers on Nov. 19 at 4 p.m. No. 5 JU (12-16) faces No. 4 West Florida (15-9) at 7 p.m. The UNF-Queens winner will play No. 2 FGCU (13-11) on Nov. 20 at 4 p.m.; and the JU-West Florida winner takes on No. 1 seed Lipscomb (19-5) at 7 p.m. The championship game is Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. This article originally appeared on Florida Times-Union: UNF senior Kaili Doctor earns school's first volleyball Player of Year

item.title: Braves Protect Polo And De Grandpre, Add Foster To 40-man
item.description: Columbus Clingstone's Cedric De Grandpre (17) pitches agains the Knoxville Smokies during a Minor League Baseball game on July 1, 2026, in Knoxville, Tennessee. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect They added right-handers Davis Polo and Cedric De Grandpre to the 40-man roster. This action shields both pitchers from being stolen in the Rule 5 Draft on Dec. 9. The team also claimed right-hander Cameron Foster off waivers from the Baltimore Orioles. These three players are no longer available to other clubs. Polo’s Rise After Surgery The 22-year-old Colombian pitcher started the year at Single-A Augusta and finished it on the major league roster. This season, he recorded 129 innings, a 27.0 percent strikeout rate, and a 3.00 ERA. His path was not smooth after Tommy John surgery late in 2024, but he found his groove. On Sept. 19, per MLB.com Braves, he delivered six scoreless innings versus Triple-A Indianapolis. His final 13 starts at four different levels produced a 2.05 ERA. De Grandpre’s Fastball Power The 24-year-old right-hander missed the 2024 season due to his own elbow surgery. He returned to pitch 129 2/3 innings with a 4.23 ERA across High-A, Double-A, and Triple-A. The radar gun recorded his fastball at 97 mph, with a sitting velocity around 95 mph. An improved slider helped him climb the ranks this year. Per reports, De Grandpre ranks as the Braves’ No. 25 prospect. He and Drue Hackenberg are the only Top 30 prospects who needed protection. Hackenberg was the only other one left off the list. Foster’s High-Whiff Upside Cameron Foster is a riskier pick but could add upside to the bullpen. Across his initial six outings for the Orioles, he managed a 9.00 ERA. Foster exhibited elevated whiff rates within his limited major league sample, per Battery Power . The Braves could implement the fix of “make hard fastball go higher in zone” highlighted in the report. He has multiple Minor League options remaining, which makes him a prime yo-yo candidate. The Winter Meetings in San Diego will host the Rule 5 Draft on Dec. 9.

According to a report from Sky Sports News journalists Rob Dorsett, James Savundra and Mark McAdam, Bournemouth are becoming increasingly receptive to selling Scott, although their valuation could reach £100m including bonuses. The 23-year-old’s contractual situation is beginning to influence discussions, with negotiations over an extension having failed to produce an agreement. Liverpool Interest Strengthened by Andoni Iraola Connection Liverpool’s pursuit of Scott carries considerable tactical significance. Iraola worked closely with the midfielder at Bournemouth, where his technical intelligence and ability to operate within demanding systems made him an important component of the Spaniard’s approach. Photo: IMAGO That familiarity could become particularly valuable as Liverpool consider how best to strengthen their midfield. Scott offers composure in possession, progressive passing and the capacity to operate across different midfield positions. His understanding of Iraola’s expectations could also reduce the adaptation period normally associated with a major signing. Sky Sports reports that Liverpool view Scott as an ideal addition capable of bringing greater creativity and passing quality to their squad. There is considerable logic behind that assessment. Liverpool’s midfield recruitment must account for the physical demands of Iraola’s football while providing the technical assurance required against opponents who defend deep. Scott appears well suited to those requirements, although the financial commitment would demand serious consideration. Arsenal and Chelsea Present Major Transfer Competition Arsenal’s interest introduces another significant complication for Liverpool. Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta have reportedly discussed their transfer strategy for 2027, with Scott emerging as a potential target. However, Arsenal would apparently need to sell an existing midfielder before completing such a substantial acquisition. Mikel Merino represents one possible departure after struggling for regular opportunities. Speaking while representing Spain, Merino explained: “We know what our roles are, and we’re both calm and eager to keep training hard to show that we can continue to be there.” He also acknowledged his frustration, stating: “Not being on the pitch most of the time isn’t ideal for a player. Arsenal is currently the best team in the world, and it’s very difficult to get minutes.” Martin Zubimendi has also been mentioned as a potential departure, although his recent performances could complicate that possibility. Chelsea remain firmly involved, with Sky Sports suggesting they possess a financial advantage over their competitors. Following Enzo Fernandez’s departure, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso remains interested in midfield reinforcements, despite Romeo Lavia’s improvement. Bournemouth Valuation Creates Liverpool Transfer Dilemma Bournemouth’s negotiating position remains substantial. Sky Sports reports that an offer worth approximately £75m to £80m, supplemented by bonuses, could potentially secure Scott’s signature. However, Bournemouth’s Europa League ambitions provide an incentive to retain him until the summer. His contract situation creates an additional complication. With Scott potentially entering the final 12 months of his agreement next summer, Bournemouth could face increasing pressure to negotiate. For Liverpool, patience may therefore offer financial advantages, although waiting would also provide Arsenal and Chelsea with opportunities to strengthen their positions. Scott’s relationship with Iraola could prove influential, particularly if the midfielder prioritises tactical familiarity and a clearly defined role. Liverpool must now determine whether that advantage warrants pursuing an expensive January agreement or waiting for a potentially more favourable summer negotiation. The outcome could reveal much about Liverpool’s recruitment priorities under Iraola and their willingness to compete financially for one of English football’s most coveted midfield talents. Our View – Anfield Index Analysis There is something genuinely appealing about Liverpool pursuing Alex Scott, particularly given his relationship with Andoni Iraola. Yet I remain uncertain whether spending anything approaching £100m on the Bournemouth midfielder represents the smartest use of the club’s resources. Scott is clearly talented. His technical ability, intelligence and familiarity with Iraola’s tactical demands make him an attractive proposition. Having a player who already understands the manager’s methods could be enormously beneficial. However, Liverpool supporters have every reason to question the proposed valuation. At £75m to £80m before bonuses, Scott would represent a considerable investment. Liverpool already possess talented midfielders, and any major expenditure should deliver an obvious improvement to the starting eleven. I also wonder whether Iraola’s admiration for Scott could influence Liverpool’s recruitment strategy too heavily. Familiarity is valuable, but the club must assess the wider market before committing such substantial resources. Arsenal and Chelsea’s involvement is concerning, particularly if Chelsea genuinely possess the strongest financial position. Liverpool cannot afford to become involved in an expensive bidding contest driven by competition rather than necessity. The contractual situation offers some encouragement. If Scott enters the final year of his Bournemouth agreement next summer, Liverpool might secure better value by waiting. For now, I would welcome his arrival, but only at a sensible price. Scott could become an excellent Liverpool player. Whether he represents an excellent Liverpool investment remains a much more difficult question.

item.title: Alcaraz defies fitness concerns to claim second win at ATP Finals
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Team Europe's Carlos Alcaraz in action against Team World's Taylor Fritz during the men's singles group stage match on day two of the Laver Cup tennis tournament at The O2. (is associated with: «Alcaraz defies fitness concerns to claim second win at ATP Finals») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Carlos Alcaraz cruised into the last four at the ATP Finals despite suffering more physical concerns. The Spaniard went into the tournament on a nine-match winning streak after collecting titles in Vienna and Paris and followed up an opening victory over Frances Tiafoe in Turin by seeing off Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4. Alcaraz is seeking his first title at the end-of-season event and looks in supreme form, but there are worries over his physical state. The Spaniard arrived in Italy looking to protect a right knee niggle and he took a medical timeout after three games of the second set to have his left hamstring taped. By that stage he was already a set and a break up against fourth seed Medvedev and he appeared untroubled in wrapping up another rapid victory. The 23-year-old admits he felt a problem with his hamstring and will assess it in the next couple of days. He said: "Well, I feel it a little bit. I'm not going to lie. I was playing great, and suddenly I felt a little problem of my hamstring, just a little bit. "I was trying to stay relaxed, to move not too aggressive. I'm thinking about being aggressive and thinking about my shots all the time. So right now I'm just feeling okay. "We will see with my team, with my physio, but I think the rest of the day and tomorrow is really going to be important days ahead of me." Alcaraz's place in the last four was sealed after Tiafoe picked up his first career win at the ATP Finals with a straights sets 7-6 (6) 6-0 win over Flavio Cobolli, which eliminated the Italian. In the doubles, Britain’s Neal Skupski and Christian Harrison claimed their first victory of the week with a 6-3, 6-4 success against Italian duo Simone Bolelli and Andrea Vavassori.

item.title: Alex Vesia’s Desired Free Agency Contract Revealed Amid Dodgers Uncertainty
item.description: ESPN’s Jeff Passan speculated how long of a deal Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Alex Vesia could land in free agency. Relievers are flying off of the shelves ahead of Dec. 1’s potential lockout, with former Dodger Evan Phillips being one of several benefactors so far. Phillips landed a three-year, $35 million deal with the Braves, and Passan believes Vesia could get a similar deal. “A few other relief pitchers should do well — and sign before the deadline… Like his ex-teammate Phillips, left-hander Alex Vesia is shooting for three years and could get it,” Passan wrote. Will Alex Vesia Get a Deal Like Evan Phillips’? Comparing Vesia and Phillips’ 2026 seasons, it’s clear that Vesia could easily land a deal similar in structure to Phillips, if not more valuable. Vesia logged a career-high 72 appearances in 2026, posting a 2.64 ERA through 58 innings while striking out 74 batters. Phillips, on the other hand, came back midway through the season after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and had a 3.46 ERA through 31 appearances. Given Vesia performed better than Phillips and is also a year younger, he is sure to command a comparable deal should he sign before the impending lockout begins. Oct 11, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Alex Vesia (51) pitches against the Milwaukee Brewers during the sixth inning in game one of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Will the Dodgers Re-Sign Alex Vesia? The Dodgers would love to have Vesia back in their ranks, but he is gaining interest from more than half of the league , meaning his market will only increase. In Dodgers Nation’s Doug McKain’s eyes, the Dodgers may not be willing to go to those lengths for a reliever. “He set himself up with a very good chance to get a big payday because he’s not coming off of Tommy John surgery, he does have durability,” McKain said , comparing Vesia’s situation to Phillips’. “Will the Dodgers keep him? They’re definitely trying but the competition of 15 teams could drive the price way beyond what they’re comfortable paying. “The Dodgers are willing to overpay on superstars… They don’t like to overpay for what they deem to be as role players and relievers that aren’t needed to get those final three outs or aren’t superstars.” If the Dodgers are to retain Vesia, they’ll have to offer him a more lucrative deal than some of the league’s top teams are offering—potentially a tall task given his current market.

item.title: SMU flips former Colorado State OL commit Jack Schein, 'I know I can develop there'
item.description: San Juan Capistrano (Calif.) JSerra offensive lineman Jack Schein visited SMU over the weekend and flipped his commitment from Colorado State to the Mustangs earlier today. Schein visited Oregon State two weeks ago before checking out SMU this past weekend. We had heard the Mustangs were in a good spot and trending for the talented tackle and Schein went ahead and pulled the trigger. “There were a lot of reasons why I chose SMU,” Schein said. “The official visit was big for me. SMU had been in touch with my coaches and following my season, so it was good to finally spend time with everybody in person. “The more I talked with the staff and got to know the guys, the easier it was to picture myself there. When I talked it through with my family after the visit, I kept coming back to how comfortable I felt around the people there and how excited I was about the chance to play for them.” Schein said development was a big part of his decision and he was comfortable with how the SMU staff and players broke it down for him. “I liked getting to spend time with the offensive linemen and hearing from them about what it’s like to play there every day,” Schein said. “With the coaches, I wanted to hear what they liked about my game and where they thought I could get better. “I appreciated how straightforward those conversations were. I left with a good sense of what they’d expect from me when I got there and how they’d help me develop as a tackle.” Schein said he’s excited about making an impact in the program. “I’m excited to get in there and compete,” Schein said. “Being at the game gave me a feel for how much people care about football at SMU, and I’m looking forward to being part of that. I’m ready to get to work with the guys up front, earn their trust, and help the team win games in the ACC.” Schein is one of the top offensive linemen out West and had a strong senior year. He has a prototype tackle frame, with a ton of length, moves well and made a big jump from his junior season in his strength and ability to finish.

item.title: Kentucky Football LB commit Sean Fox receives his 5th star
item.description: Another Kentucky Football commit just received his fifth star! Sean Fox is now a 5-star in 247 Sports’ updated rankings and climbed to No. 21 nationally. That makes him Kentucky’s highest-rated commit in the 2027 class at 247 Sports. This comes a couple of days after Kentucky quarterback commit Jake Nawrot received his fifth star at Rivals, where he’s currently ranked No. 17 nationally, making him the highest-ranked UK pledge at any recruiting service. Fox currently plays at Warren Central in Indianapolis, Indiana, and committed to Kentucky on June 25, 2026. Tony Washington was the primary recruiter for the elite linebacker and did an incredible job landing him over Clemson and Georgia. With his 6-foot-5 frame, Fox is a tall and long defensive star. Andrew Ivins of 247 Sports said Fox “could be molded into a variety of different things.” Defensive coordinator Jay Bateman is going to have some fun having such an incredible weapon on his defense in the coming years. This coaching staff has prioritized certain guys and landed them, which has gotten Kentucky’s class ranked No. 13 in America. The committee’s loyalty to Alabama looked even harder to justify given how it handled Indiana just a week earlier. The defending national champions went into their Week 10 bye at No. 4 and came out of it at No. 9, with committee chair Hunter Yurachek chalking up the five-spot drop to a packed weekend that featured seven games within the top 25. Yurachek called Indiana “ probably the victim of having a bye week at the wrong time ,” but that explanation did little to placate Curt Cignetti, who spent the following days needling the committee over the slide. Whatever my next show/ game is I try to be better. With the CFP show it seems like it’s the opposite. Every week they one up themselves with ridiculous reasoning and rankings. — Jake Butt (@Jbooty88) November 18, 2026 Butt is far from the first to roll his eyes at the weekly ESPN reveal, which has drawn growing criticism over who the rankings show is really serving , but few have put it quite as colorfully as he did in his next post. “The sky is green” they said. But I can see with my own eyes the sky is blue..? “The sky is green.” ••••••••••••• “There is no SEC bias” they said. — Jake Butt (@Jbooty88) November 18, 2026 As Butt pointed out in another post, there’s a lot more than pride on the line when the committee gets these rankings wrong, and the stakes are about to grow considerably. ESPN and the CFP made the 24-team playoff official earlier this month, with the network agreeing to pay an extra $345 million a year on top of the $1.3 billion it already spends on the event. With conference championship games going away to make room for the bigger bracket, where a team lands in the rankings — and whether that means a bye, a home game or a favorable first-round draw — is about to matter more than ever. There is way to much on the line to allow these rankings to play out like this. Literally, tens of millions of $$$. You have legacies, history, jobs are on the line. CFP success effects admissions and university revenue. It effects branding. With home CFP games you get an additional major revenue boost. This effects recruiting and the portal. I could go on and on. I don’t understand how there can be consensus to this level, yet nothing will change. Even next year when we go to 24.. you can manipulate rankings leading to a bye, a home field advantage, or a favorable matchup. There’s way to much on the line to allow this level of subjectivity to drive the rankings. — Jake Butt (@Jbooty88) November 18, 2026 Butt’s concerns about subjectivity aside, the Big Ten is far from frozen out, with undefeated UCLA sitting pretty at No. 4 and Ohio State jumping six spots to No. 14 at 7-3 as one of six conference teams in the top 25. But there are only two rankings shows left before the bracket is set on Dec. 6, and unless the committee comes up with a better explanation than the ones it’s offered so far, Butt seems ready to keep insisting the sky is blue. item.title: ESPN insider reveals when Lamar Jackson might return from injury for Ravens
item.description: ESPN insider reveals when Lamar Jackson might return from injury for Ravens originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens are having a bit of a nightmare season right now, as Lamar Jackson is out for a long time due to a serious thumb injury, while they've dropped a few games and now sit at 4-6. But thanks to the 6-4 Cleveland Browns occupying the final Wild Card spot, Baltimore has a real chance of making a comeback and making a playoff run. That's why they acquired Jacoby Brissett. While the season feels like it's just about over, ESPN's Dan Graziano revealed a huge update on when Jackson could come back from IR. This timeline gives the Ravens a clear stretch where, if they can stay alive, their playoff hopes might not be over just yet. Ravens might get Lamar Jackson back in Week 16 "They play the Browns again in Week 16, which is on the shorter end of Lamar Jackson's injury recovery timetable, but they believe there's a chance he could be back around that time if all goes well," Graziano writes. It's still very much up in the air if Jackson will return at all this season, but the optimistic outlook could have Jackson returning to the offense in Week 16 when the Ravens face the Browns again this season. If the Ravens can stay alive in the playoff hunt, and make up a game or two on the Browns over Weeks 11, 12, 14 and 15, then there's a chance Jackson is back to help the Ravens to make a push for the playoffs. To justify bringing Jackson back, they're going to need to win some of these next few games. They face off against the Carolina Panthers , Houston Texans , Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and Pittsburgh Steelers between now and Week 16. MORE : Derrick Henry posts stunning rushing numbers as Ravens suffer embarrassing loss Will they be able to go at least 2-2 in those games? After losing to the Los Angeles Chargers , and Derrick Henry ran for 10 yards on 10 attempts, there's reason to doubt if this team can still contend. But if they remain in contention and get Jackson back, with matchups against the Browns, Cincinnati Bengals , and Steelers to close out the season, Jackson returning to the team would be a huge boon for the offense. Ravens fans shouldn't celebrate that Jackson might be coming back just yet, as it's way too soon to tell when he'll return. But a Week 16 return does open the door for some hope for Baltimore amid an incredibly disappointing season. The Kansas City Royals could turn to free agency to fill their opening at third base after trading Maikel Garcia, with Alec Bohm emerging as one suggested option. Wednesday’s six-player deal with the Seattle Mariners brought Kansas City three pitchers but left the club needing to replace Garcia. FanSided’s Robert Murray identified Bohm as a potential fit while discussing the Royals’ next move. He offered the idea without reporting negotiations or confirmed interest. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Foul Territory shared Murray’s comments Wednesday on X, formerly Twitter, in a clip from “The Robert Report” exploring Kansas City’s options. “And you guys mentioned Isaac Paredes as a possible trade option, like the name that came to my mind was Alec Bohm. He’s a free agent now. Obviously, was with Philadelphia for the past few seasons. First half of last season was not necessarily the greatest. He had a lot of stuff obviously going on off the field, but he really improved in the second half of the season. He had a really strong end, and from what I gather, he’s got a really strong market here.” There's a lot to like on both sides of the Maikel Garcia trade, @ByRobertMurray explains… Could the Royals entertain Alec Bohm after trading Maikel Garcia? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/PjZT37m8yQ — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) November 18, 2026 Bohm finished 2026 with a .249/.315/.383 batting line, 15 home runs and 88 RBI across 155 games for the Philadelphia Phillies. His production improved after the All-Star break. Following a .215/.278/.354 first half, he batted .298 with a .794 OPS in the second half. The Phillies did not extend him a qualifying offer, meaning a signing would not require Kansas City to surrender draft picks. The Royals received right-handers Bryce Miller and Logan Evans and left-handed reliever Jose Ferrer in the Garcia trade. Right-handers James McArthur and LP Langevin also went to Seattle. Garcia hit .268 with three home runs and 38 RBI in 82 games during an injury-interrupted season. Adding Bohm would address the vacancy through free agency, allowing Kansas City to keep the pitching depth it acquired Wednesday. item.title: Portugal’s new No 7 Forbs channels Ronaldo for winner as Wales are denied
item.description: One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese Football Federation put it. For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia and Herzegovina – who knocked them out of World Cup qualifying this year – all potential opponents in Friday’s draw in Switzerland. Afterwards Craig Bellamy stressed the importance of keeping elite company to accelerate improvement but reiterated that he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, after which his contract expires. item.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future
item.description: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA’s chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 44-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4bn) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the players’ union for England and Wales observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money. item.title: Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable
item.description: The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments. There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the 4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows. Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling
item.description: Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling. Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days , Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer . He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. item.description: Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding In the final, absurdly tense moments before England finally did it and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: s omehow, anyhow . What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too. Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. item.title: AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership
item.description: Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can When you walk up from Haydons Road railway station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium. AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter – but that makes running a loss‑making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board, which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.” Continue reading...

item.title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number
item.description: Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
